name: Split Flap
tagline: Mechanical split-flap letters that clatter through the alphabet before spelling your message.
description: Launch and announcement style built on split-flap (Solari) letters. Black flap cells with a hairline split, cream condensed type and amber labels; each character flips through the letters before it, its top half folding down in 3D, staggered across the board, with green and blinking amber status words as the only colour. The preview is a station departure board whose rows shuffle up before it re-flips to spell the product name.

display.usage: Flap characters 600 at 64px centred in 48×80px cells on a 53px pitch; board title 700 at 64px; column heads and labels 22–26px tracked 0.2em

body.usage: Amber ticker strip 32px tracked 0.16em, scrolling at 140px/s

easing.flip: linear halves: top flap rotateX 0→-90°, then bottom flap 90→0°, 0.065s per character

transitions: no cuts: the board itself is the transition, re-flipping row by row
departure: the top row leaves and every row re-flips to the next row's content
finale re-flip staggers outward from the centre column
textAnimations: each cell flips through 3–8 preceding drum characters (deterministic per cell) before landing
phase stagger: 0.014–0.016s per column + 0.09–0.1s per row; finale 0.022s per column from centre
BOARDING blinks at 1.2Hz once its flaps settle; ON TIME is green, CANCELLED dimmed
station clock second hand sweeps, minute hand jumps on the minute

rhythm.notes: Three board states in 8s: departures at 0.5s, rows shuffle at 3.7s, product reveal at 5.6s. Each re-flip takes ~1.2s of clatter, then the board holds while the clock, ticker and blinking status keep it alive.

guide:
- Look only: build the user's own subject in this visual language; don't reuse the example's scene.
- All type is mechanical: every character lives in its own 48×80px flap cell (#1c1c1e top, darker bottom, 5px radius) with a 2px black split line and tiny hinge pins, on a 53px pitch inside a #0a0a0a housing (18px radius) with a #26282b bezel, over a #15171a wall with a soft top light. Never use LED dots or glowing pixels.
- Characters are Barlow Condensed 600 at 64px in #efece4; headings 700 at 64px; labels and column heads 22–26px tracked 0.2em in amber #ffb000 or grey #7c7a74.
- Flip by rendering from time: top half (old char) rotates 0→-90° from its bottom edge, then the bottom half (new char) rotates 90→0° from its top edge, 0.065s per character, perspective ~340px. Drive it from one timeline proxy's onUpdate so every frame is seekable.
- Characters walk the drum (" A–Z 0–9 : . - ·"), passing 3–8 letters before the target; pick the count from the cell index, never Math.random(). Stagger 0.014–0.016s per column and 0.09–0.1s per row; a re-flip takes ~1.2s of clatter.
- No cuts: the board itself is the transition. Each new beat re-flips the board to new content, then holds while small things keep it alive (a ticking clock, an amber ticker scrolling at ~140px/s, a blinking status).
- Colour is rare: only status words get it, green #3ddc84 for good, amber blinking at 1.2Hz for live, dimmed #8d8a83 for cancelled.
- Optional motif: a departure-board layout (TIME / DESTINATION / PLAT / STATUS, blank cells as gutters) whose rows describe the subject as metaphors, with the top row leaving and the rest shuffling up.
- Optional motif: a final re-flip staggered outward from the centre column (0.022s per column) to spell the name in white, a tagline in amber and a URL in green, with the column heads faded to 20%.
example: The preview is a train-station departure board for a product release: rows like SHIPPED and CODE REVIEW clatter into place, the top train departs and the rows shuffle up, then the board re-flips to spell the product name. Don't copy this scene unless asked.
